NKJV.1: So Abijah rested with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of David. Then Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days the land was quiet for ten years.
NKJV.2: Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God,
NKJV.3: for he removed the altars of the foreign gods and the high places, and broke down the sacred pillars and cut down the wooden images.
NKJV.4: He commanded Judah to seek the LORD God of their fathers, and to observe the law and the commandment.
NKJV.5: He also removed the high places and the incense altars from all the cities of Judah, and the kingdom was quiet under him.
NKJV.6: And he built fortified cities in Judah, for the land had rest; he had no war in those years, because the LORD had given him rest.
NKJV.7: Therefore he said to Judah, “Let us build these cities and make walls around them, and towers, gates, and bars, while the land is yet before us, because we have sought the LORD our God; we have sought Him, and He has given us rest on every side.” So they built and prospered.
NKJV.8: And Asa had an army of three hundred thousand from Judah who carried shields and spears, and from Benjamin two hundred and eighty thousand men who carried shields and drew bows; all these were mighty men of valor.
NKJV.9: Then Zerah the Ethiopian came out against them with an army of a million men and three hundred chariots, and he came to Mareshah.
NKJV.10: So Asa went out against him, and they set the troops in battle array in the Valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.
NKJV.11: And Asa cried out to the LORD his God, and said, “LORD, it is nothing for You to help, whether with many or with those who have no power; help us, O LORD our God, for we rest on You, and in Your name we go against this multitude. O LORD, You are our God; do not let man prevail against You!”
NKJV.12: So the LORD struck the Ethiopians before Asa and Judah, and the Ethiopians fled.
NKJV.13: And Asa and the people who were with him pursued them to Gerar. So the Ethiopians were overthrown, and they could not recover, for they were broken before the LORD and His army. And they carried away very much spoil.
NKJV.14: Then they defeated all the cities around Gerar, for the fear of the LORD came upon them; and they plundered all the cities, for there was exceedingly much spoil in them.
NKJV.15: They also attacked the livestock enclosures, and carried off sheep and camels in abundance, and returned to Jerusalem.

ESV.1: Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David. And Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days the land had rest for ten years.
ESV.2: And Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God.
ESV.3: He took away the foreign altars and the high places and broke down the pillars and cut down the Asherim
ESV.4: and commanded Judah to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, and to keep the law and the commandment.
ESV.5: He also took out of all the cities of Judah the high places and the incense altars. And the kingdom had rest under him.
ESV.6: He built fortified cities in Judah, for the land had rest. He had no war in those years, for the LORD gave him peace.
ESV.7: And he said to Judah, “Let us build these cities and surround them with walls and towers, gates and bars. The land is still ours, because we have sought the LORD our God. We have sought him, and he has given us peace on every side.” So they built and prospered.
ESV.8: And Asa had an army of 300,000 from Judah, armed with large shields and spears, and 280,000 men from Benjamin that carried shields and drew bows. All these were mighty men of valor.
ESV.9: Zerah the Ethiopian came out against them with an army of a million men and 300 chariots, and came as far as Mareshah.
ESV.10: And Asa went out to meet him, and they drew up their lines of battle in the Valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.
ESV.11: And Asa cried to the LORD his God, “O LORD, there is none like you to help, between the mighty and the weak. Help us, O LORD our God, for we rely on you, and in your name we have come against this multitude. O LORD, you are our God; let not man prevail against you.”
ESV.12: So the LORD defeated the Ethiopians before Asa and before Judah, and the Ethiopians fled.
ESV.13: Asa and the people who were with him pursued them as far as Gerar, and the Ethiopians fell until none remained alive, for they were broken before the LORD and his army. The men of Judah  carried away very much spoil.
ESV.14: And they attacked all the cities around Gerar, for the fear of the LORD was upon them. They plundered all the cities, for there was much plunder in them.
ESV.15: And they struck down the tents of those who had livestock and carried away sheep in abundance and camels. Then they returned to Jerusalem.

NASB.1: So Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David, and his son Asa became king in his place. The land was undisturbed for ten years during his days.
NASB.2: Asa did good and right in the sight of the LORD his God,
NASB.3: for he removed the foreign altars and high places, tore down the [sacred] pillars, cut down the Asherim,
NASB.4: and commanded Judah to seek the LORD God of their fathers and to observe the law and the commandment.
NASB.5: He also removed the high places and the incense altars from all the cities of Judah. And the kingdom was undisturbed under him.
NASB.6: He built fortified cities in Judah, since the land was undisturbed, and there was no one at war with him during those years, because the LORD had given him rest.
NASB.7: For he said to Judah, 'Let us build these cities and surround [them] with walls and towers, gates and bars. The land is still ours because we have sought the LORD our God; we have sought Him, and He has given us rest on every side.' So they built and prospered.
NASB.8: Now Asa had an army of 300,000 from Judah, bearing large shields and spears, and 280,000 from Benjamin, bearing shields and wielding bows; all of them were valiant warriors.
NASB.9: Now Zerah the Ethiopian came out against them with an army of a million men and 300 chariots, and he came to Mareshah.
NASB.10: So Asa went out to meet him, and they drew up in battle formation in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.
NASB.11: Then Asa called to the LORD his God and said, 'LORD, there is no one besides You to help [in the battle] between the powerful and those who have no strength; so help us, O LORD our God, for we trust in You, and in Your name have come against this multitude. NASB.12: So the LORD routed the Ethiopians before Asa and before Judah, and the Ethiopians fled.
NASB.13: Asa and the people who [were] with him pursued them as far as Gerar; and so many Ethiopians fell that they could not recover, for they were shattered before the LORD and before His army. And they carried away very much plunder.
NASB.14: They destroyed all the cities around Gerar, for the dread of the LORD had fallen on them; and they despoiled all the cities, for there was much plunder in them.
NASB.15: They also struck down those who owned livestock, and they carried away large numbers of sheep and camels. Then they returned to Jerusalem.

NLT.1: When Abijah died, he was buried in the City of David. Then his son Asa became the next king. There was peace in the land for ten years.
NLT.2: Asa did what was pleasing and good in the sight of the LORD his God.
NLT.3: He removed the foreign altars and the pagan shrines. He smashed the sacred pillars and cut down the Asherah poles.
NLT.4: He commanded the people of Judah to seek the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and to obey his law and his commands.
NLT.5: Asa also removed the pagan shrines, as well as the incense altars from every one of Judah’s towns. So Asa’s kingdom enjoyed a period of peace.
NLT.6: During those peaceful years, he was able to build up the fortified towns throughout Judah. No one tried to make war against him at this time, for the LORD was giving him rest from his enemies.
NLT.7: Asa told the people of Judah, “Let us build towns and fortify them with walls, towers, gates, and bars. The land is still ours because we sought the LORD our God, and he has given us peace on every side.” So they went ahead with these projects and brought them to completion.
NLT.8: King Asa had an army of 300,000 warriors from the tribe of Judah, armed with large shields and spears. He also had an army of 280,000 warriors from the tribe of Benjamin, armed with small shields and bows. Both armies were composed of well-trained fighting men.
NLT.9: Once an Ethiopian named Zerah attacked Judah with an army of 1,000,000 men and 300 chariots. They advanced to the town of Mareshah,
NLT.10: so Asa deployed his armies for battle in the valley north of Mareshah.
NLT.11: Then Asa cried out to the LORD his God, “O LORD, no one but you can help the powerless against the mighty! Help us, O LORD our God, for we trust in you alone. It is in your name that we have come against this vast horde. O LORD, you are our God; do not let mere men prevail against you!”
NLT.12: So the LORD defeated the Ethiopians in the presence of Asa and the army of Judah, and the enemy fled.
NLT.13: Asa and his army pursued them as far as Gerar, and so many Ethiopians fell that they were unable to rally. They were destroyed by the LORD and his army, and the army of Judah carried off a vast amount of plunder.
NLT.14: While they were at Gerar, they attacked all the towns in that area, and terror from the LORD came upon the people there. As a result, a vast amount of plunder was taken from these towns, too.
NLT.15: They also attacked the camps of herdsmen and captured many sheep, goats, and camels before finally returning to Jerusalem.

WEB.1: So Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in David’s city; and Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days, the land was quiet ten years.
WEB.2: Asa did that which was good and right in Yahweh his God’s eyes;
WEB.3: for he took away the foreign altars and the high places, broke down the pillars, cut down the Asherah poles,
WEB.4: and commanded Judah to seek Yahweh, the God of their fathers, and to obey his law and command.
WEB.5: Also he took away out of all the cities of Judah the high places and the sun images; and the kingdom was quiet before him.
WEB.6: He built fortified cities in Judah; for the land was quiet, and he had no war in those years, because Yahweh had given him rest.
WEB.7: For he said to Judah, “Let us build these cities, and make walls around them, with towers, gates, and bars. The land is yet before us, because we have sought Yahweh our God. We have sought him, and he has given us rest on every side.” So they built and prospered.
WEB.8: Asa had an army of three hundred thousand out of Judah who bore bucklers and spears, and two hundred eighty thousand out of Benjamin who bore shields and drew bows. All these were mighty men of valor.
WEB.9: Zerah the Ethiopian came out against them with an army of a million troops and three hundred chariots, and he came to Mareshah.
WEB.10: Then Asa went out to meet him, and they set the battle in array in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.
WEB.11: Asa cried to Yahweh his God, and said, “Yahweh, there is no one besides you to help, between the mighty and him who has no strength. Help us, Yahweh our God; for we rely on you, and in your name are we come against this multitude. Yahweh, you are our God. Don’t let man prevail against you.”
WEB.12: So Yahweh struck the Ethiopians before Asa and before Judah; and the Ethiopians fled.
WEB.13: Asa and the people who were with him pursued them to Gerar: and so many of the Ethiopians fell that they could not recover themselves; for they were destroyed before Yahweh and before his army; and they carried away very much booty.
WEB.14: They struck all the cities around Gerar; for the fear of Yahweh came on them, and they plundered all the cities; for there was much plunder in them.
WEB.15: They also struck the tents of livestock, and carried away sheep in abundance, and camels, and returned to Jerusalem.

CSB17.1: Abijah rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of David. His son Asa became king in his place. <sup>ⓘ</sup> During his reign the land experienced peace for ten years.
CSB17.2: Asa did what was good and right <sup>ⓙ</sup> in the sight of the LORD his God.
CSB17.3: He removed the pagan altars and the high places. He shattered their sacred pillars and chopped down their Asherah poles. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.4: He told the people of Judah to seek the LORD God of their ancestors and to carry out the instruction and the commands.
CSB17.5: He also removed the high places and the shrines <sup>[1]</sup> from all the cities of Judah, <sup>ⓛ</sup> and the kingdom experienced peace under him.
CSB17.6: Because the land experienced peace, Asa built fortified cities in Judah. <sup>ⓜ</sup> No one made war with him in those days because the LORD gave him rest. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.7: So he said to the people of Judah, “Let’s build these cities and surround them with walls and towers, with doors and bars. <sup>ⓐ</sup> The land is still ours because we sought the LORD our God. We sought him and he gave us rest on every side.” So they built and succeeded.
CSB17.8: Asa had an army of three hundred thousand from Judah bearing large shields and spears, <sup>ⓑ</sup> and two hundred eighty thousand from Benjamin bearing regular shields and drawing the bow. All these were valiant warriors.
CSB17.9: Then Zerah the Cushite came against them with an army of one million men and three hundred <sup>[2]</sup> chariots. They came as far as Mareshah.
CSB17.10: So Asa marched out against him and lined up in battle formation in Zephathah Valley at Mareshah. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.11: Then Asa cried out to the LORD his God: <sup>ⓓ</sup> “LORD, there is no one besides you to help the mighty and those without strength. Help us, LORD our God, for we depend on you, <sup>ⓔ</sup> and in your name we have come against this large army. LORD, you are our God. Do not let a mere mortal hinder you.”
CSB17.12: So the LORD routed the Cushites before Asa and before Judah, <sup>ⓕ</sup> and the Cushites fled.
CSB17.13: Then Asa and the people who were with him pursued them as far as Gerar. <sup>ⓖ</sup> The Cushites fell until they had no survivors, for they were crushed before the LORD and his army. So the people of Judah carried off a great supply of loot.
CSB17.14: Then they attacked all the cities around Gerar because the terror of the LORD was on them. <sup>ⓗ</sup> They also plundered all the cities, since there was a great deal of plunder in them.
CSB17.15: They also attacked the tents of the herdsmen and captured many sheep and camels. Then they returned to Jerusalem.

AMP.1: So Abijah slept with his fathers [in death], and they buried him in the City of David; and Asa his son became king in his place. The land was at peace for ten years during his days.
AMP.2: Asa did what was good and right in the sight of the LORD his God.
AMP.3: He removed the foreign altars and high places and tore down the [pagan] pillars (obelisks, memorial stones), and cut to pieces the Asherim [the symbols of the goddess Asherah].
AMP.4: And he commanded Judah to seek the LORD God of their fathers [to inquire of and for Him and seek Him as a vital necessity], and to observe the law [given to Moses] and the commandment.
AMP.5: Asa also removed the [idolatrous] high places and the incense altars from all the cities of Judah. The kingdom was at rest and undisturbed under his reign.
AMP.6: He built fortified cities in Judah, since the land was at rest, and there was no one at war with him in those years, because the LORD had given him rest.
AMP.7: So he said to Judah, "Let us build these cities and surround them with walls, towers, gates and bars [to secure the doors]. The land is still ours because we have sought the LORD our God; we have sought Him [longing for Him with all our heart] and He has given us peace on every side." So they built and prospered.
AMP.8: Now Asa had an army of 300,000 men from Judah, who carried large shields and spears, and 280,000 from Benjamin, who carried shields and drew bows, all courageous men.
AMP.9: Now Zerah the Ethiopian (Cushite) came out against Judah with an army of a million men and three hundred chariots, and he came as far as Mareshah.
AMP.10: Then Asa went out against him, and they drew up in battle formation in the Valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.
AMP.11: Asa called out to the LORD his God, saying, "O LORD, there is no one besides You to help in the battle between the powerful and the weak; so help us, O LORD our God, for we trust in and rely on You, and in Your name we have come against this multitude. O LORD, You are our God; let not man prevail against You."
AMP.12: So the LORD struck the Ethiopians [with defeat] before Asa and Judah, and the Ethiopians fled.
AMP.13: Asa and the people who were with him pursued them as far as Gerar; and so many Ethiopians fell that none of them were found alive; for they were destroyed before the LORD and His army. And they carried away a very large amount of spoil.
AMP.14: They attacked and destroyed all the cities around Gerar, for the dread of the LORD had fallen on them. They plundered all the cities, for there was a large amount of spoil in them.
AMP.15: They also struck down the people [living] in tents who had livestock, and took captive large numbers of sheep and camels. Then they returned to Jerusalem.

MSG.1:
Abijah died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Asa became the next king.
For ten years into Asa's reign the country was at peace.
MSG.2: Asa was a good king. He did things right in God's eyes.
MSG.3: He cleaned house: got rid of the pagan altars and shrines, smashed the sacred stone pillars, and chopped down the sex-and-religion groves (Asherim).
MSG.4: He told Judah to center their lives in God, the God of their fathers, to do what the law said, and to follow the commandments.
MSG.5: Because he got rid of all the pagan shrines and altars in the cities of Judah, his kingdom was at peace.
MSG.6: Because the land was quiet and there was no war, he was able to build up a good defense system in Judah. God kept the peace.
MSG.7: Asa said to his people, "While we have the chance and the land is quiet, let's build a solid defense system, fortifying our cities with walls, towers, gates, and bars. We have this peaceful land because we sought God; he has given us rest from all troubles." So they built and enjoyed prosperity.
MSG.8: Asa had an army of 300,000 Judeans, equipped with shields and spears, and another 280,000 Benjaminites who were shield bearers and archers. They were all courageous warriors.
MSG.9: Zerah the Ethiopian went to war against Asa with an army of a million plus 300 chariots and got as far as Mareshah.
MSG.10: Asa met him there and prepared to fight from the Valley of Zephathah near Mareshah.
MSG.11: Then Asa prayed to God, "O God, you aren't impressed by numbers or intimidated by a show of force once you decide to help: Help us, O God; we have come out to meet this huge army because we trust in you and who you are. Don't let mere mortals stand against you!"
MSG.12: God defeated the Ethiopians before Asa and Judah; the Ethiopians ran for their lives.
MSG.13: Asa and his men chased them as far as Gerar; so many of the Ethiopians were killed that there was no fight left in them—a massacre before God and his troops; Judah carted off loads of plunder.
MSG.14: They devastated all the towns around Gerar whose people were helpless, paralyzed by the fear of God, and looted the country.
MSG.15: They also attacked herdsmen and brought back a lot of sheep and camels to Jerusalem.

NIV.1: And Abijah rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David. Asa his son succeeded him as king, and in his days the country was at peace for ten years.
NIV.2:
Asa King of Judah
Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the Lord his God.
NIV.3: He removed the foreign altars and the high places, smashed the sacred stones and cut down the Asherah poles.
NIV.4: He commanded Judah to seek the Lord, the God of their fathers, and to obey his laws and commands.
NIV.5: He removed the high places and incense altars in every town in Judah, and the kingdom was at peace under him.
NIV.6: He built up the fortified cities of Judah, since the land was at peace. No one was at war with him during those years, for the Lord gave him rest.
NIV.7: “Let us build up these towns,” he said to Judah, “and put walls around them, with towers, gates and bars. The land is still ours, because we have sought the Lord our God; we sought him and he has given us rest on every side.” So they built and prospered.
NIV.8: Asa had an army of three hundred thousand men from Judah, equipped with large shields and with spears, and two hundred and eighty thousand from Benjamin, armed with small shields and with bows. All these were brave fighting men.
NIV.9: Zerah the Cushite marched out against them with a vast army and three hundred chariots, and came as far as Mareshah.
NIV.10: Asa went out to meet him, and they took up battle positions in the Valley of Zephathah near Mareshah.
NIV.11: Then Asa called to the Lord his God and said, “Lord, there is no one like you to help the powerless against the mighty. Help us, O Lord our God, for we rely on you, and in your name we have come against this vast army. O Lord, you are our God; do not let man prevail against you.”
NIV.12: The Lord struck down the Cushites before Asa and Judah. The Cushites fled,
NIV.13: and Asa and his army pursued them as far as Gerar. Such a great number of Cushites fell that they could not recover; they were crushed before the Lord and his forces. The men of Judah carried off a large amount of plunder.
NIV.14: They destroyed all the villages around Gerar, for the terror of the Lord had fallen upon them. They plundered all these villages, since there was much booty there.
NIV.15: They also attacked the camps of the herdsmen and carried off droves of sheep and goats and camels. Then they returned to Jerusalem.

NET.1: (13:23) Abijah passed away and was buried in the City of David. His son Asa replaced him as king. During his reign the land had rest for ten years.
NET.2: (14:1) Asa did what the LORD his God desired and approved.
NET.3: He removed the pagan altars and the high places, smashed the sacred pillars, and cut down the Asherah poles.
NET.4: He ordered Judah to seek the LORD God of their ancestors and to observe his law and commands.
NET.5: He removed the high places and the incense altars from all the cities of Judah. The kingdom had rest under his rule.
NET.6: He built fortified cities throughout Judah, for the land was at rest and there was no war during those years; the LORD gave him peace.
NET.7: He said to the people of Judah: “Let’s build these cities and fortify them with walls, towers, and barred gates. The land remains ours because we have followed the LORD our God and he has made us secure on all sides.” So they built the cities and prospered.
NET.8: Asa had an army of 300,000 men from Judah, equipped with large shields and spears. He also had 280,000 men from Benjamin who carried small shields and were adept archers; they were all skilled warriors.
NET.9: Zerah the Cushite marched against them with an army of 1,000,000 men and 300 chariots. He arrived at Mareshah,
NET.10: and Asa went out to oppose him. They deployed for battle in the Valley of Zephathah near Mareshah.
NET.11: Asa prayed to the LORD his God: “O LORD, there is no one but you who can help the weak when they are vastly outnumbered. Help us, O LORD our God, for we rely on you and have marched on your behalf against this huge army. O LORD our God, don’t let men prevail against you!”
NET.12: The LORD struck down the Cushites before Asa and Judah. The Cushites fled,
NET.13: and Asa and his army chased them as far as Gerar. The Cushites were wiped out; they were shattered before the LORD and his army. The men of Judah carried off a huge amount of plunder.
NET.14: They defeated all the cities surrounding Gerar, for the LORD caused them to panic. The men of Judah looted all the cities, for they contained a huge amount of goods.
NET.15: They also attacked the tents of the herdsmen in charge of the livestock. They carried off many sheep and camels and then returned to Jerusalem.
